notes:
SEGMENT SCOPE: Arunachal Pradesh (st-ar), Manipur (st-mn), Meghalaya (st-ml) states complete except districts (owned by local-lgd, referenced by st-<code>-dist-* ids already present in data/raw/local-lgd.json). Meghalaya's three Sixth Schedule Autonomous District Councils (in-khadc-khasi-hills, in-jhadc-jaintia-hills, in-ghadc-garo-hills) are owned by local-lgd and only referenced here (via Governor oversight relations).

KEY FINDINGS / CURRENT-EVENTS VERIFICATION (as of 2026-09-25):
- Manipur: President's Rule (Article 356), imposed 13 Feb 2025 after N. Biren Singh's resignation amid the 2023-25 ethnic conflict, was REVOKED on 4 February 2026 when Yumnam Khemchand Singh (BJP) was sworn in as CM heading a BJP-NPP-NPF-JD(U) coalition with 2 Deputy CMs. This was cross-checked across three independent fetches (Wikipedia 'Manipur', 'Chief Minister of Manipur', 'Yumnam Khemchand Singh', and the 'Yumnam Khemchand Singh ministry' infobox/table, which is the primary source for the full 5-member council of ministers list).
- Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya CMs (Pema Khandu, Conrad Sangma) are unchanged incumbents; no 2025-26 election was due in either (AR last elected Apr 2024, ML Feb 2023 - see MINISTRIES quality-bar election list, neither state was in the 2025-26 batch).
- Meghalaya's council of ministers was reshuffled/expanded on 16 September 2025 (BJP's Sanbor Shullai and several NPP/UDP/HSPDP MLAs inducted); this data reflects that post-reshuffle composition.

TOOLING NOTE: WebSearch had already exhausted its shared per-session budget (200/200, consumed by sibling segments before this segment ran) — all research here was done via WebFetch (Wikipedia pages + official *.gov.in / *.nic.in portals) and curl+Wikipedia parse-API for bulk tables (rate-limited intermittently, presumably by concurrent sibling segments; worked after backing off). No browser tools were used, per instructions.

KNOWN GAPS (declared, not guessed):
1. State Human Rights Commission current chairpersons for all three states could not be confirmed (no dedicated Wikipedia pages found, official portals not checked exhaustively, and WebSearch was unavailable) - positions included with holder:null, confidence:low. Existence of AR's SHRC itself is not 100% certain (NHRC's list page was ambiguous on its constitution date); MN (est. 2003) and ML (est. 2016-07) are confirmed to exist.
2. State Election Commissioner titles for Manipur and especially Meghalaya are sourced from Wikipedia's SEC pages which use the term 'Chief Electoral Officer' - this may be the page's own imprecision (conflating the Union ECI-appointed CEO, who runs Lok Sabha/Assembly polls, with the Article 243K State Election Commissioner, who runs local-body polls). Included at medium/low confidence with the ambiguity flagged in notes; needs a State Gazette or SEC-portal cross-check.
3. Chief Secretary and DGP holder details (batch/cadre years, exact appointment dates) are thin - only current name + IAS/IPS status was verifiable from official portals in the time available; no appointment dates found.
4. Manipur PSC Chairman shown vacant per Wikipedia's table (last recorded change: retirement 4 Oct 2023) - not independently re-confirmed for 2026; could plausibly have been filled since.
5. Legislative Assembly party-wise strength for all three states reflects each Assembly's own Wikipedia infobox at time of research; by-election churn between now and 2026-09-25 was not independently checked seat-by-seat.
6. No Legislative Council exists in AR, MN or ML (only UP/Bihar/Maharashtra/Karnataka/AP/Telangana have one per the task brief), so none was modelled - this is a scope confirmation, not a gap.
7. Meghalaya has NO municipal corporation - only the Shillong Municipal Board (a lower-tier municipal board under the Meghalaya Municipal Act 1973, last held elections in 2000) and other ULBs, which are aggregated under local-lgd's st-ml-urban-local-bodies entity; no separate municipal_corporation entity was created for Meghalaya to avoid inventing one.
8. Full district-by-district member/MLA rosters were not captured (out of scope for this segment; SCHEMA asks for Council of Ministers with portfolios, which was captured in full for all three states, not every backbench MLA).

ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION ADDENDUM (2026-09-25): Independently re-checked 44 positions (all 3 Governors, all 3 CMs, all 5 Deputy CMs, all 21 captured cabinet ministers across AR/MN/ML, all 3 Speakers/Deputy Speakers/Leaders of Opposition, Meghalaya's Chief Secretary via the official portal, and the AR/MN PSC chair status) against fresh Wikipedia and official-portal fetches (WebSearch budget was still exhausted at verification time, so WebFetch + curl on Wikipedia/official portals was used, per tooling note). Every holder, since-date, party and vacancy status already in this file matched the fresh sources exactly - no factual corrections to holder data were needed. Also cross-checked the three in-pos-mp-rs-<code>-1 relation targets against data/raw/parliament-rajya-sabha.json - all three IDs exist there with matching naming convention (no dangling reference). Ran a structural pass (python): zero duplicate IDs, zero unresolved parentId/orgId/headPositionId/appointedBy/onAdviceOf references, all kind/rank/relation-type values are within SCHEMA.md's allowed sets, and the file round-trips through json.load/json.dump cleanly.
Two items flagged for follow-up (not corrected here, since neither can be resolved without inventing facts): (a) Manipur's Council of Ministers as captured (CM + 2 Deputy CMs + 2 ministers = 5) is below the Article 164(1A)/91st Amendment constitutional minimum of 12 ministers for a 60-seat assembly; this is not a data error - it is what the Yumnam Khemchand Singh ministry Wikipedia page (the freshest available source) actually shows as of this check - but it strongly suggests either a real cabinet expansion since Feb 2026 that Wikipedia has not yet recorded, or a genuine constitutional anomaly worth flagging; needs a news-source check once WebSearch budget is available. (b) Could not independently confirm or deny the three State Human Rights Commission chairperson vacancies (already confidence:low in this file) or the AR SHRC's very existence - the candidate Wikipedia pages for 'Arunachal Pradesh State Human Rights Commission' and 'List of State Human Rights Commissions in India' both 404. Left as-is (confidence low, holder null) per the never-invent rule.
Coverage note: the High Courts serving these states are judiciary-owned and correctly not redefined here; for completeness - Arunachal Pradesh is served by the Itanagar Permanent Bench of the Gauhati High Court (in-hc-gauhati), Manipur by the Manipur High Court (in-hc-manipur), and Meghalaya by the Meghalaya High Court (in-hc-meghalaya); no relation edge was added since SCHEMA.md's relation-type list (elects/appoints/advises_appointment/administers/oversees/accountable_to/...) has no type that fits 'is served by' court jurisdiction, and inventing one was out of scope for this verification pass.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh
entities.description: A Himalayan border state in India's Northeast bordering Bhutan, China (disputed McMahon Line) and Myanmar; became a full state in 1987 after being a Union Territory. Governed under a Governor-Chief Minister system with a single-chamber legislature.

entities.name: Government of Arunachal Pradesh
entities.description: The executive government of Arunachal Pradesh, headed by the Governor as constitutional head and the Chief Minister as head of government.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh Council of Ministers
entities.description: The Chief Minister and cabinet ministers collectively responsible to the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly; currently the Fifth Pema Khandu ministry, sworn in 13 June 2024.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly
entities.description: The unicameral 60-seat legislature of Arunachal Pradesh, elected for 5-year terms by first-past-the-post.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh State Election Commission
entities.description: Constitutional body under Article 243K/243ZA conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions and municipalities in Arunachal Pradesh.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh Public Service Commission
entities.description: Recruits candidates for civil services and other state government posts in Arunachal Pradesh under Article 315.

entities.name: Arunachal Pradesh State Human Rights Commission
entities.description: State-level statutory human rights body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; current chairperson could not be confirmed from available sources.

entities.name: Lokayukta of Arunachal Pradesh
entities.description: State anti-corruption ombudsman institution for Arunachal Pradesh established under the state Lokayukta Act.

entities.name: Itanagar Municipal Corporation
entities.description: The sole municipal corporation of Arunachal Pradesh, covering the state capital Itanagar; established 2013.

entities.name: Manipur
entities.description: A Northeast Indian state bordering Myanmar, home to the Meitei-majority Imphal Valley and surrounding Naga/Kuki-Zo hill districts. President's Rule (Article 356) was in force from 13 February 2025 to 4 February 2026 following ethnic violence and the resignation of CM N. Biren Singh; an elected government resumed office on 4 February 2026.

entities.name: Government of Manipur
entities.description: The executive government of Manipur. President's Rule was revoked on 4 February 2026 when the Yumnam Khemchand Singh ministry (BJP-led NDA coalition) was sworn in.

entities.name: Manipur Council of Ministers
entities.description: The Yumnam Khemchand Singh ministry, sworn in 4 February 2026 as a BJP-NPP-NPF-JD(U) NDA coalition, succeeding a year of President's Rule.

entities.name: Manipur Legislative Assembly
entities.description: The unicameral 60-seat (12th) Assembly of Manipur, elected 28 February - 5 March 2022; continued to exist (unlike the ministry) through the 2025-26 President's Rule period.

entities.name: Manipur State Election Commission
entities.description: Constitutional body under Article 243K/243ZA conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions and municipalities in Manipur.

entities.name: Manipur Public Service Commission
entities.description: Recruits candidates for civil services and other state government posts in Manipur under Article 315. Chairman post has been vacant since October 2023 per Wikipedia's last-updated listing.

entities.name: Manipur State Human Rights Commission
entities.description: State-level statutory human rights body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; constituted in 2003. Current chairperson could not be confirmed from available sources.

entities.name: Lokayukta of Manipur
entities.description: State anti-corruption ombudsman institution for Manipur.

entities.name: Imphal Municipal Corporation
entities.description: The sole municipal corporation of Manipur, covering the state capital Imphal; upgraded from Imphal Municipal Council in 2014. Mayor's post vacant per Wikipedia as of last update (no elections held since 2016 local body poll term ended).

entities.name: Meghalaya
entities.description: A Northeast Indian state carved out of Assam in 1972, home to the matrilineal Khasi, Jaintia and Garo peoples. Most of the state is Sixth Schedule tribal area governed in part by three Autonomous District Councils alongside the elected state government.

entities.name: Government of Meghalaya
entities.description: The executive government of Meghalaya, headed by the Governor and a Chief Minister leading the Meghalaya Democratic Alliance (NPP-BJP-UDP-HSPDP) coalition.

entities.name: Meghalaya Council of Ministers
entities.description: The Second Conrad Sangma ministry, sworn in 7 March 2023 as an NPP-led Meghalaya Democratic Alliance coalition (NPP, BJP, UDP, HSPDP), reshuffled/expanded 16 September 2025.

entities.name: Meghalaya Legislative Assembly
entities.description: The unicameral 60-seat legislature of Meghalaya, elected 27 February 2023; seats are drawn roughly 29 Khasi Hills, 7 Jaintia Hills, 24 Garo Hills.

entities.name: Meghalaya State Election Commission
entities.description: Constitutional body under Article 243K/243ZA conducting elections to District Councils and municipal/local bodies in Meghalaya.

entities.name: Meghalaya Public Service Commission
entities.description: Recruits candidates for civil services and other state government posts in Meghalaya under Article 315.

entities.name: Meghalaya State Human Rights Commission
entities.description: State-level statutory human rights body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; constituted July 2016. Current chairperson could not be confirmed from available sources.

entities.name: Lokayukta of Meghalaya
entities.description: State anti-corruption ombudsman institution for Meghalaya.
